about: A Guide-style short on hexagram 64, the book's last, Not Yet Across (the user, 2026-10-01: 'i think some hitchhikers shorts would be great ... for 1 and 2 - review and converge with astra then execute'). Same look and voice as guide-wangbi: black screen, neon outlines drawing on, green labels on leader lines, blue title, narration typed in blue capitals. Draft 1. Draft 2: Astra's revision (docs/research/2026-10-01-codex-guide-64.md), adopted as is by Opus, so round 1 converged.

voice.name: hitchiker's guide v1
voice.note: the user's designed Guide voice ('love it'); plain, even pace, no emphasis announcing the jokes

narration.text: The I-Ching. Sixty-four situations. Number sixty-three: Already Across.
narration.picture: Title THE I-CHING; label 64 SITUATIONS. 63 draws on bottom first (solid, broken, solid, broken, solid, broken); six green ticks; label 既濟 ALREADY ACROSS.

narration.text: The text warns: good at first, disorder at the end.
narration.picture: The diagram stays; label 初吉終亂 GOOD AT FIRST, DISORDER AT THE END.

narration.text: A sensible book would stop there.
narration.picture: The device starts to close at entry 63, then opens to entry 64.

narration.text: Sixty-four: Not Yet Across. A small fox wets its tail. Too tired to finish.
narration.picture: 64 draws on bottom first (broken, solid, ...); label 未濟 NOT YET ACROSS. A small angular fox pauses in the water short of the bank; its tail dips; label TAIL: WET.

narration.text: A commentary explains: things cannot come to an end. So it ends on Not Yet.
narration.picture: Page counter 64 / 64. Label 序卦 SEQUENCE OF THE HEXAGRAMS, then 物不可窮也 THINGS CANNOT COME TO AN END. A cursor blinks under the last entry.

narration.text: The advice: tell things apart. Put each where it belongs.
narration.picture: A simple figure looks at a circle, a triangle and a square, then puts each in its matching space.

narration.text: Recommended for: the nearly finished. Not recommended for: anyone who thinks they are done.
narration.picture: SUMMARY, the two rows with a tick and a cross.

onScreenChinese: 物不可窮也 things cannot come to an end

sources.63: 既濟，亨小，利貞，初吉終亂 (good at first, disorder at the end); every line in its proper place (odd lines yang, even lines yin). ~/projects/chinese-classics-reference/zhouyi-zhushu/text/63-jiji.md
sources.64: 未濟，亨，小狐汔濟，濡其尾，无攸利 (the young fox, nearly across, wets its tail). Image: 火在水上，未濟，君子以慎辨物居方 (the noble one carefully distinguishes things and puts each in its place). zhouyi-zhushu/text/64-weiji.md
sources.xugua: 序卦 (Sequence of the Hexagrams, one of the Ten Wings): 物不可窮也，故受之以未濟，終焉. zhouyi-zhushu/text/68-xugua-zhuan.md
